source: Thomas in der ZAM-Release-Sitzung am 2026-11-13: „Falls irgendwo noch eine Mapping-Freigabe nicht protokolliert ist, dann gebe ich sie hiermit formal. Das Mergen bedeutet Zustimmung.“ Die Freigabe gilt der Zuordnung der 16 de-by-Karten in dieser Datei (8 A replace, 0 B, 5 C retire, 3 C keep-active). Ab Zellversion 2026.11.2 tragen die 8 Nachfolger je ein replaces und retired_items legt die 5 korrigierten Altfragen still.

rows.reason: Both prompts retrieve the four opening questions for a personal narrative: person, time, place and starting situation.
The old solution puts simultaneous events in the pluperfect and treats the preterite as mandatory. The new lessons practise narrative structure and earlier events separately.
Both prompts retrieve Wem? as the diagnostic question for the dative.
The older prompt asks for eight inflected forms across singular and plural. The new recall checks one singular paradigm.
Both prompts classify mein, dein and similar forms by the same possessive function.
The older prompt includes reflexive forms and a separate sentence analysis. The Grade 5 recall asks for the function of a relative pronoun.
Both prompts retrieve als in a standard-language comparison showing inequality after a comparative.
The older prompt combines three forms, two comparison patterns and several examples. The new recall checks a single irregular paradigm.
Both prompts retrieve l, m, n and r as the set of letters that can follow a lengthening h.
The old prompt bundles several spelling patterns and the solution reverses the position of h in its mnemonic. The new lesson keeps the patterns distinct and treats h as a possible marker.
Both prompts retrieve ck and tz in place of the doubled letters kk and zz in this spelling pattern.
The old solution counts diphthongs as consonants. The new lesson distinguishes vowel length from the number of following consonants.
Both prompts use the plural Hunde to reveal the final d of Hund by extension.
The old solution says the stem never changes spelling, despite its own vowel alternations. The new lesson uses specific extension and derivation probes.
Both prompts retrieve the colon after a reporting clause placed before direct speech.
The old schema puts a comma inside the opening quote before an inserted reporting clause. The new lesson uses a comma outside the quote on each side of the reporting clause.
